title.narrative: ENHANCING MARKET BASED SOLUTIONS FOR ENDANGERED BIODIVERSITY CONSERVATION IN TWO WATERSHEDS OF THE CAUCA VALLEY COLOMBIA

description.narrative: This project will enhance connectivity between forest blocks and provide additional food and shelter for several endangered bird species including the Cauca Guan (Penelope perspicax), Indigo-winged Parrot (Hapalopsittaca fuertesi), Brown-banded Antpitta (Grallaria milleri) and Turquoise Dacnis (Dacnis hartlaubi). Project activities will take place within two watersheds in Colombias Cauca Valley, the Amaime-Sonso Watershed in the department of Valle del Cauca, and the Chinchin - Ro Claro watershed in Caldas department. The intended outcome is to enhance the biodiversity value of regenerative agriculture, specifically silvopastoral systems, by improving tree and shrub selection with higher biodiversity value alongside plants that supplement cattle feed. Clearing land for cattle production is the biggest threat to habitat loss in the Americas, but silvopastoral systems offer a balanced solution that can increase farmer profits while reducing soil erosion, improving water security, sequestering carbon and improving biodiversity conservation and climate resilience for many species. The project also will support local livelihoods through improved profits for small to medium sized farms and through the creation of community-based tree nurseries to support the restoration activities.
